one_liner: WHATWG-compliant C++20 URL parser used by Node.js; about 7.8x faster than libcurl's URL API on real-world URLs.
what_it_does: Ada parses, validates and normalizes URLs under the WHATWG URL Standard, the browser model. That includes UTS #46/IDNA host processing and percent-encoding. It also ships URLSearchParams, URLPattern and an experimental URLPattern list router. The main call is `ada::parse<ada::url_aggregator>(input, base*)`, which returns a `tl::expected<url, ada::errors>` with getters and setters that mirror the JavaScript `URL` object; there is also `ada::can_parse` for validation only and a C API in `ada_c.h`. It does not replace `curl_url_set`/`curl_url_get` line for line: the interface is different and the normalized output follows WHATWG rules, not RFC 3986.
how_it_is_fast: The default `url_aggregator` writes the normalized URL into one `std::string` and tracks the components as 32-bit offsets. The buffer is reserved up front, rounded to the next power of two, so getters return `string_view`s and do no allocation. A fast path (`try_parse_simple_absolute` / `try_parse_simple_relative`) skips the full WHATWG state machine for URLs that are already canonical. On main, that path classifies 16 bytes at a time with nibble-table lookups (SSSE3 `pshufb` / NEON `tbl`, with an SSE2 fallback). Elsewhere Ada uses vectorized tab/newline scans (SSSE3, NEON, SSE2, LoongArch LSX, RISC-V RVV, and a 64-bit SWAR fallback), 256-entry constexpr lookup tables for delimiters and forbidden host code points, and a branchless perfect hash to detect special schemes. The paper reports up to 8x fewer instructions than curl and 3x fewer than servo rust-url.
when_to_use: Servers, proxies, crawlers or log pipelines that normalize or validate millions of URLs and want output identical to a browser's or Node's `new URL()`.
Replacing a hot-path libcurl `CURLU` parse-plus-serialize step when WHATWG normalization (punycode hosts, percent-encoded paths) is acceptable or wanted.
Validation-only filtering with `ada::can_parse`: the v4 release post reports 28.1 ns/URL on a ~100k-URL dataset (Apple M5 Max).
Embedding a spec-compliant URL implementation in a JavaScript runtime or polyglot stack: Ada has a C API plus official Rust, Go, Python and Kotlin bindings.
Route matching with URLPattern or the experimental URLPattern list, with the regex engine of your choice plugged in.
when_not_to_use: You need RFC 3986 behavior or byte-exact round-trips. Ada rewrites hosts to punycode and percent-encodes paths, and it accepts a different set of URLs from curl (on the top100 corpus, curl rejects 130 URLs and Ada 26).
Your toolchain is older than C++20. The README lists GCC 12+, LLVM 14+ and Visual Studio 2022 as tested.
Your input is not UTF-8 (UTF-16 or Latin-1 strings from a JS engine, for example). The code base assumes UTF-8, and issue #77 about other encodings is still open.

Binary size is tight. An issue thread (#900) puts the compiled library at around 500 KB, mostly IDNA/Unicode tables. URLPattern can be turned off with `ADA_INCLUDE_URL_PATTERN=OFF`, but the maintainers say the Unicode support cannot be removed.
You need HTTP request-line or header parsing. Ada only parses URLs.

integration.form: static lib or shared lib (CMake, SOVERSION 4), or source-drop of the amalgamated ada.h + ada.cpp
integration.dependencies: none (simdutf is optional via ADA_USE_SIMDUTF; tests and benchmarks fetch their own dependencies through CPM)
integration.min_toolchain: C++20; tested with GCC 12+, LLVM 14+ and MSVC 2022; CMake 3.16+
integration.platforms: any C++20 target. SIMD paths: x86-64 (SSE2 baseline, SSSE3 scanners, optional AVX-512 BW/VL/VBMI2 IPv4 kernel chosen at compile time), aarch64 NEON, LoongArch LSX, RISC-V RVV, with a scalar SWAR fallback. CI covers Ubuntu x86-64 and ARM64, s390x and loongarch64 under QEMU, Windows MSVC/clang-cl, and macOS.
integration.thread_safety: Not documented. `parse` is a free function that returns an owned value. The only global state found is the max-input-length limit, a relaxed `std::atomic` that applies to the whole process. Concurrent mutation of one URL object is not addressed.

gotchas: `url_aggregator` getters return `string_view`s into the internal buffer, and any setter invalidates them. The header warns against passing a getter's result into a setter on the same object without copying it first. C API `ada_string` values are borrowed in the same way.
Check the parse result before dereferencing it. The README calls `url->get_href()` on a failed parse unsafe.
`ada::set_max_input_length` is process-wide. When the limit is exceeded, the `void` setters (`set_search`, `set_hash`) do nothing and give no signal.

Release and main differ. v4.0.0 (2026-07-27) bumped SOVERSION to 4 and now rejects some inputs it used to accept. The README Quick Start still downloads v3.0.0 single-header files. The August 2026 SIMD fast-path work (PRs #1214/#1216) is on main only. On main, GCC/Clang x86-64 builds compile those scanners with `target("ssse3")`, and I found no runtime CPU check, so CPUs without SSSE3 may fault.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: ada-rs (Rust) and lucid-url both benchmark against C++ Ada. They claim small wins on small corpora (7.4% on 9 URLs; 1.27x for Url but slower for UrlAggregator), and sorug is a Rust WHATWG parser measured only against servo url. Pick Ada when you need C/C++ integration, full web-platform-test compliance, fuzzing coverage and a production record (Node.js, Cloudflare Workers).
verified_claims_summary: Ada's own Google Benchmark harness parses each URL in the top100 corpus and reads back the normalized href. The README reports 188 ns/URL for Ada, 664 for servo rust-url and 1471 for curl's `curl_url_set` + `curl_url_get`, on an 'Apple MacBook 2022' with LLVM 14 and unstated flags. The curl run reuses one handle but allocates the href string for every URL. The peer-reviewed paper shows the same gap on an AMD EPYC 7262 (GCC 11) and an Apple M2 (Apple/LLVM 14): above 3M and 5M URLs/s for Ada, against about 0.5M and nearly 1M for curl 7.81.0.
status_note: Actively maintained: last commit 2026-09-20, v4.0.0 released 2026-07-27, with ABI-check CI and fuzzing in CI (CIFuzz plus past OSS-Fuzz reports). It is dual-licensed Apache-2.0/MIT and easy to vendor as two amalgamated files.
